<div align="center">
    <h1>
        Zabbix SMSEagle Media Type
    </h1>
    <h4>
        SMS &amp; voice-call notifications via SMSEagle with two-way ACK
    </h4>
    <br>
</div>
<br>
<br>

<!-- *********************************************************************************************************************************** -->
<!-- *** BODY ************************************************************************************************************************** -->
<!-- *********************************************************************************************************************************** -->
## Description
SMSEagle notification media types for Zabbix - send alerts as **SMS** or as a **voice call**
(text-to-speech) through an [SMSEagle](https://www.smseagle.eu) hardware SMS gateway via its REST
API v2. Agentless webhook, no external scripts.

This package contains two media types:
- **SMSEagle SMS** - SMS notifications (`type=sms`).
- **SMSEagle Voice** - voice call with advanced TTS (`type=tts_adv`). Set `type` to `tts_adv,sms`
  to also send an accompanying ACK-instruction SMS together with the call.

## Two-way ACK (acknowledge by SMS)
> [!NOTE]
> Inbound acknowledge requires **SMSEagle firmware 6.31 or newer** (released 2026-06-01), which
> added the native `POST (Zabbix ACK)` webhook method ("Webhooks: added integration for Zabbix API
> ACK"). On older firmware the outgoing ACK instruction in the alert messages still works, but the
> reply is not processed automatically.

The problem message contains: `For ACK please respond with message: ACK {EVENT.ID} <message>`.
A recipient replies with `ACK eventid <message>` - the event ID is mandatory, the `<message>` is
optional (Zabbix `<...>` notation) - and the problem is acknowledged in Zabbix.

Inbound handling is done natively by SMSEagle - no custom receiver needed. In the SMSEagle UI under
**Webhooks**, add a rule with:
- **URL method**: `POST (Zabbix ACK)`
- **URL**: the full path to your Zabbix API endpoint `api_jsonrpc.php`, e.g.
  `https://zabbix.example.com/api_jsonrpc.php` (or `https://zabbix.example.com/zabbix/api_jsonrpc.php`
  if Zabbix runs under a `/zabbix` sub-path)
- **API key of your service**: a Zabbix API token belonging to a user allowed to acknowledge problems
- **Send request when**: Always send, **Send request for**: Incoming message

## Requirements
- **Zabbix 7.0 or higher**
- SMSEagle device with REST API v2 and an API access token
- Network access from the Zabbix server/proxy to the SMSEagle device

## Setup
### 1. Create an SMSEagle API access token
In the SMSEagle web UI open **Users**, pick (or create) a dedicated user and click
**Access to API**:
1. Select **APIv2**.
2. Click **Generate new token** and copy the value.
3. Under **Manage allowed API methods** enable only what is needed (least privilege):
   - **Messages -> Send SMS** (`POST`) - required for the SMS media type
   - **Calls -> Make a TTS Advanced call** (`POST`) - required for the Voice media type
   - if you use the `tts_adv,sms` switch on the Voice media type, enable **both** of the above
4. **Save**.

This token goes into the `access_token` parameter of the media type. It is a different token from
the Zabbix API token used for the two-way ACK above.

### 2. Find the voice ID (Voice media type only)
`voice_id` is device-specific - it depends on the TTS voices installed on your SMSEagle. In the UI
go to **Calls -> TTS Voice models** and use the number from the **ID** column for the desired
language/voice (online voices are under **Calls -> TTS Online voice models**). Example IDs differ
per device, e.g. `4` = Czech, `1` = German, `2`/`3` = English.

### 3. Import and configure the media types
1. Import [`mediatype-SMSEagle-by-initMAX.yaml`](./7.0/mediatype-SMSEagle-by-initMAX.yaml) into
   **Alerts -> Media types**.
2. On each media type set:
   - `url` - your SMSEagle URL (e.g. `https://10.10.0.100`)
   - `access_token` - the token from step 1
   - `http_proxy` - optional, leave empty unless the webhook must go through an HTTP proxy
   - (Voice) `voice_id` - the ID from step 2
3. Assign the media type to users (**Users -> Users -> Media**). The recipient (`{ALERT.SENDTO}`)
   accepts: a phone number, `<id>:c` for a Phonebook contact, or `<id>:g` for a Phonebook group
   (comma-separated for multiple).
4. Use the media type in your **Trigger actions**.

| Parameter | Description | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `url` | SMSEagle device base URL - no trailing slash and no API path (the webhook appends `/api/v2/...`). Example: `https://10.10.0.100` or `https://sms.company.com` | - |
| `access_token` | SMSEagle APIv2 access token (see step 1) | - |
| `http_proxy` | HTTP proxy for the webhook request. **Empty = no proxy is used.** Example: `http://proxy.company.com:3128` | (empty) |
| `type` | Notification channel: `sms` or `tts_adv` (advanced TTS voice call), or both comma-separated e.g. `tts_adv,sms`. (`tts` = legacy basic TTS call, `mms` = multimedia - **not suitable for Zabbix alerts**) | per media type |
| `voice_id` | TTS voice ID (Voice only) - device-specific, see **Calls -> TTS Voice models** | - |
| `priority` | Outbox queue priority. `0` = normal; a higher number is sent ahead of normal-priority messages when the queue is busy | `0` |
| `flash` | Flash SMS (`true`/`false`) - shown straight on the recipient's screen and not stored in their inbox | `false` |

> The remaining parameters (`encoding`, `modem_no`, `oid`, `date`, `send_after`, `send_before`,
> `duration`, `test`) are advanced/optional - leave them at the defaults unless you have a specific
> need.
